legacy.original_title: 1.2 - Adopt the game-kit contract for state, actions, and rules
legacy.body:
## Summary

Implement the shared `game-kit` contract so Sudoku exposes one deterministic
game core for the client, solver, and training.

## Context

`src/lib.rs` is a one-line comment and `Cargo.toml` does not depend on
`tools/game-kit`. The Python solver in `bots/solver/` has no shared contract with
the Rust core.

## Expected outcome

- `sudoku` implements `game_kit::Game`.
- State and action types are explicit and serializable.
- `apply` is deterministic and rejects illegal placements.
- `legal_actions` respects row, column, and box constraints.
- The core has no browser or rendering code.

## Out of scope

- Puzzle generation.
- Python solver changes.
- Browser UI.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `Cargo.toml` depends on a pinned `game-kit` version.
- [ ] `State`, `Action`, and `Game` are implemented.
- [ ] Illegal placements return `None` and never panic.
- [ ] Replaying the same puzzle and moves produces identical state.
- [ ] A conformance test covers initial state, legal actions, and apply.
- [ ] The state can be exported for the solver.

## Plan

- [ ] Map Sudoku rules to the traits.
- [ ] Add serialization.
- [ ] Add the conformance test.
- [ ] Document invariants in `docs/`.

## Validation

- [ ] Same puzzle + moves = same state hash.
- [ ] A conflicting placement is rejected.
- [ ] `cargo test` passes.

## References

- Shared contract: tools/game-kit
- Boundaries: ops/templates#31
- Shared contracts: ops/templates#32
- Tests: ops/templates#34
